I'm a clean person. I'm messy, but I'm clean. I sometimes don't make my bed for a week, but I'll never leave my dishes in the sink overnight and I hang up wet towels. I sweep my kitchen nightly and mop it twice a week, but I'll leave my clean dishes in the dishwasher for a day or so. But money is tight, so I decided I move in with a roommate to make life easier, plus the apartment wouldn't be in my name (I'm moving in three months and need somewhere to live in the meantime).

No. Bad. Never again.

My new roommate was the beastiest of obeasts. So loud, so proud, and so messy. At first I just cleaned the kitchen weekly, amazed at how many dishes we were using in such a short amount of days (I assumed she'd clean the kitchen on Tuesdays and I'd clean it on Fridays, because I understand not everybody has my standards of cleanliness), and amazed by how many half-filled cups of soda were lying around. This girl must have friends over all day while I'm at work, I thought.

Nope. Not even.

They were all hers. She'd go out to eat and bring home a cup of soda, set it somewhere, and never go back for it. Wow, thinks I, how gross. But I overlooked it because I'm nice, and because she was supposedly helping me keep things clean.

Except one day I called in sick and ended up staying in the apartment all day in my room with the curtains drawn. I wasn't being creepy-creepy, I was trying to not throw up from bright lights. I overheard her talking with a friend about how she'd never do something she could get somebody else to do, and how she hadn't had to clean the apartment since I'd moved in.

I, in my sickness-fueled rage, stumbled across r/fph (except v/fph now, you know, but it was r/fph back then). SWEET SWEET FREEDOM! THERE ARE OTHERS LIKE ME! I'M NOT ALONE IN MY SUFFERING!

I stopped cleaning up her messes. I did my dishes, and that's it. I lived for work, I'd come home and sleep, and leave for work again in the morning. The apartment became filthy in less than a week. She complained to me, asking why I wasn't cleaning anymore since that was part of the agreement to let me live there (it wasn't, we were equal-cleaners and I was paying 50/50). I said I was too busy with work, but surely she could pick up the slack until I could get a handle on things. She got miffed, so neither of us cleaned. I hated every moment. Everything stunk.

I moved out shortly thereafter, and no longer live with anybody outside a healthy BMI. Things are clean and lovely again. I can only imagine the chaos and filth in which my former housemate currently lives.
